role: THE ONLY register of what currently blocks external beta. §266 made it the single authoritative P0/P1/P2 closure register for Safety InSite v1.0 controlled human beta. Historical RELEASE_BLOCKERS.md and REMAINING_BLOCKERS.md files under verification/ are historical evidence of blockers that were live at the time; they are not current status and must not be read as such.
scope: the WHOLE Safety InSite v1.0 product as a controlled-beta candidate, not only the Expert HazLenz layer. §266 widened it from the Expert-only scope §263 established.

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: The shipped §265 frontend hardcodes requestVersion: 1, but the Expert panel only renders once a deterministic analysis exists, and that analysis already occupies requestVersion 1. Every Expert run from the real workflow is refused.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: HTTP 409 'A newer analysis request already exists.'; execution row ANALYSIS_FAILED / PERSISTENCE_CONFLICT; 1 provider leg spent BEFORE the refusal.
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: Expert is unusable in the product it was built for, and each attempt spends real money on a hosted leg to reach a conflict. In beta this is both a broken feature and an uncapped cost per retry.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: Allocate requestVersion server-side, or have the client send max(existing requestVersion) + 1 the way the deterministic path already does at frontend-next/app/inspection-workspace/page.tsx:1410. Server-side allocation is preferred: a client-chosen version is a client-chosen collision.
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: an integration case that runs Expert on an observation that ALREADY carries a deterministic analysis — the case §265's suite never exercised, because every §265 case used a fresh observation.

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: Expert and deterministic analyses share one per-observation requestVersion sequence and one status='current' slot in hazlenz_analyses. A successful Expert run marks the deterministic analysis superseded and becomes 'current' itself.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: after Expert at requestVersion 2: client_supplied row status='superseded', server_authored row status='current'.
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: The workspace restores the newest non-superseded analysis and casts its resultSnapshot to HazLenzAnalysisResult (page.tsx:778, 855, 969, 1814). After any Expert run it therefore restores an EXPERT snapshot into the deterministic UI — the HazLenz step degrades to blanks and analysisId points subsequent reviews at the Expert analysis. It also means an ADVISORY layer supersedes the customer-authoritative record, which inverts invariant 30 at the data level.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: Make producer-scoped currency explicit: readers of the deterministic flow must filter to producer='client_supplied', and supersession must not cross producers. Do not redesign the shared table — scope the reads and the supersession.
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: restore-after-Expert-run renders the deterministic analysis unchanged
blocksExternalBetaNow.introducedBy: §261 (shared currency); first reachable by a user at §265

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: The production image cannot run migrations and nothing runs them at boot. migrationsRun:false; start:render does not migrate; the only migration script is typeorm-ts-node-commonjs against src/, and neither ts-node nor src/ exists in the runtime image. Code can therefore deploy ahead of schema.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: §256 recorded production applied through 1800000018000. The branch carries 1800000019000 (ExpertAnalysisAuthorityFoundation) and 1800000020000 (ExpertHumanConfirmation), both unapplied.
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: Deploying this branch against the current production schema breaks far more than Expert. The HazLenzAnalysis entity now declares producer, analysisState, confirmationRequired, expertExecutionId (019000) and settlementReviewId (020000); TypeORM selects all of them, so EVERY read of hazlenz_analyses fails — including the core deterministic finalizeFinding path. Render autoDeploy is on, so a push is the trigger.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: Add a migration step that runs against the COMPILED datasource — typeorm is already a production dependency and dist/database/{data-source,migrations} are already in the image, so `typeorm -d dist/database/data-source.js migration:run` works. Run it as a release command BEFORE the new code serves traffic, and record the applied version.
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: a deploy rehearsal on a disposable database proving migrate-then-serve ordering

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: No Terms of Use and no Privacy Policy exist. /legal is still a 120-line disclaimer. Registration still gates on a single acceptedTerms checkbox evaluated client-side at register/page.tsx:79 — it is never transmitted and never persisted.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: unchanged since §256; no terms or privacy route exists under frontend-next/app
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: Real inspectors would enter real workplace safety observations, and real photographs, under no contract, no liability limitation, no data-handling disclosure and no recorded consent. There is no evidence any user ever agreed to anything.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: Beta Terms and a Privacy Notice, plus server-side recording of the acknowledgement (who, what version, when).
blocksExternalBetaNow.owner: legal + product owner; engineering can only wire the consent record
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: both documents published and an acceptance row persisted at registration

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: Observation text leaves the product to a third-party model provider and nothing user-facing says so. /legal carries a trademark disclaimer only.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: no disclosure of third-party processing anywhere in frontend-next/app/legal
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: Undisclosed third-party processing of customer workplace content. This is the single most likely source of a legitimate beta-user complaint.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: disclosure in the Privacy Notice; name the processing, not necessarily the vendor
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: the published privacy notice states it

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: Report generation returns 500 in every environment checked, because no object storage is configured.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: neither STORAGE_S3_BUCKET nor STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT is set
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: No report, no photo evidence, no PDF. §266 also establishes that this now GATES BOOT rather than only failing at runtime: validate-production-environment requires STORAGE_S3_BUCKET, so production cannot start without it. That is the right behaviour and it makes provisioning a hard precondition of deployment rather than a surprise.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: provision the bucket and set STORAGE_S3_* in a section authorized to do so
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: one upload and one download round-trip against the provisioned bucket

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: No per-workspace or per-user spend ceiling exists, and there is no targeted Expert kill switch. The cost-accounting columns on expert_analysis_executions (firstPassInputTokens, firstPassOutputTokens, verifierInputTokens, verifierOutputTokens, costUsd) are never populated by the product path, because the transport seam ExpertLegResponse carries only { ok, toolInput, failureKind, detail } and drops usage.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: no product-path writer for any usage column; ExpertLegResponse has no usage field; no EXPERT_ENABLED-style flag exists anywhere in src.
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: Beta cost is unbounded and unattributable. §255 measured material per-analysis cost and an unconditional verifier leg. Existing controls are a 10/60s per-caller throttle, a 180s per-leg timeout, max_tokens 8000, and pre-spend idempotency — which bound RATE but not TOTAL.
blocksExternalBetaNow.mitigationThatExistsToday: unsetting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY disables Expert and degrades to ANALYSIS_FAILED, which the product renders honestly as 'could not be reached... not a finding that there are no hazards'. That is a real, product-safe kill switch, but it needs a restart and it is not a first-class control. Revoking the fullSafeScope grant is NOT an Expert kill switch: it also disables /safescope-v2/classify, the deterministic path.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: carry usage back through the transport seam and persist it; add a per-workspace daily analysis ceiling enforced server-side; add an explicit Expert enable flag.
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: a workspace that hits the ceiling is refused before the provider is reached

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: No error-monitoring or structured-logging dependency exists in either workspace. Observability is console output plus /health, /health/live, /health/ready and /health/version.
blocksExternalBetaNow.measured: no sentry/datadog/otel/pino/winston dependency in backend or frontend package.json
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: A beta whose stated purpose is learning from real use would run blind. Nothing would tell the team that analyses are failing, that users are stuck awaiting confirmation, that settlement is erroring, or that authorization failures are spiking. The product already writes rich security_audit_events and expert_analysis_executions rows — the data exists; nothing surfaces it.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: minimum: backend error reporting with release tagging, plus one operational query or dashboard over expert_analysis_executions (failures, awaiting-confirmation age) and security_audit_events (entitlement_denied, authorization failures).
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: an induced failure appears in the monitoring surface within one minute

blocksExternalBetaNow.statement: The entire Expert product integration is local-only. HEAD is 9 commits ahead of origin/main and 0 behind. Nothing deployed can contain any of it.
blocksExternalBetaNow.consequence: There is no deployable commit for the beta candidate, and the controlled-beta candidate must be traceable to exactly one. This also explains why production's schema being applied only through 018000 is currently CONSISTENT: production has neither the code nor the schema.
blocksExternalBetaNow.requiredAction: push the candidate branch, then decide the deploy commit deliberately — with Render autoDeploy ON, pushing to the deployed branch IS deploying.
blocksExternalBetaNow.dependency: NO_PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_MECHANISM must close first, or the push deploys code ahead of schema
blocksExternalBetaNow.closureProof: one named SHA, confirmed by GET /health/version against the running instance

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: GET /inspections/:id returns observations.analyses unfiltered — including server_authored Expert rows in any state, with resultSnapshot whole. The route carries JwtGuard only: no fullSafeScope entitlement, no effectiveDecision, no authorityStatement, no confirmationRequired framing.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.measured: the probe read snapshotKind=EXPERT_HAZLENZ_SERVER_AUTHORED_ANALYSIS and posture=CONTINUE_WITH_CONTROLS from GET /inspections/:id; entitlement guard ABSENT.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.whyNotP0Today: no consumer renders it. The frontend reads observation.analyses only to restore the deterministic analysis, and the report PDF's extractStandard cannot read an Expert snapshot because it looks for executiveJudgment / standardsReasoning / primaryCitation, none of which an Expert snapshot has. So an unsettled proposal does not BECOME an authoritative product fact today.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.whyItStillMatters: this is the bypass §260 section 11 was written to prevent, and it is invisible: a future feature could render resultSnapshot.posture from the inspection payload with no compiler error, no runtime error and no guard. The §265 frontend authority boundary covers the Expert routes, not this one.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.requiredAction: filter server_authored rows out of the inspection payload, or project them through the same authority shape the Expert read route uses.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.closureProof: GET /inspections/:id carries no raw Expert posture

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: canonical-reports.service.snapshotInspection copies observation.analyses verbatim into the persisted report snapshot, unfiltered by producer or state.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.whyNotP0: generation requires inspection.status='completed', which requires every active finding finalized or dismissed, which the §265 guard now gates. The snapshot is data at rest: the report list and detail routes deliberately exclude sourceSnapshot, and the PDF renderer cannot extract Expert shapes.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.requiredAction: exclude server_authored rows from the report snapshot, or project them

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: The §265 downstream guard runs before the finalized/dismissed branch, so it refuses a DISMISSAL of a finding whose review cites an unsettled Expert analysis.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.whyItMatters: dismissing a finding asserts that there is no finding — it consumes no operational conclusion — so requiring settlement first is over-restriction, and §260 section 11 blocked 'finding finalization' on the grounds that finalization asserts a settled conclusion. A dismissal does not. It also traps the user: a dismissed finding is how an inspection reaches completion, so the reviewer must settle a classification for a hazard they are rejecting.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.requiredAction: product-owner decision, then either move the guard after the dismissal branch or state deliberately that dismissal is gated too.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.note: raised under the standing rule that every safety remediation is checked for overcorrection

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: Of the six §260 section 11 consumers, one is explicitly guarded. §266 established by import analysis that the other five do not consume Expert analyses at all.

classificationPerConsumer.completionReadinessAndTransition: NOT APPLICABLE — evaluateCompletionReadiness reads findings and reviews only and never touches hazlenz_analyses. It is nonetheless TRANSITIVELY_CONTAINED in effect, because completion requires every active finding finalized or dismissed and finalization is guarded.
classificationPerConsumer.correctiveActionCreation: NOT APPLICABLE — upsertCorrectiveActionForFinding runs only on the finalized branch, inside the guarded method, and reads the review's conclusion.
classificationPerConsumer.reportFinalizationAndExport: TRANSITIVELY_CONTAINED, with the caveat recorded as EXPERT_SNAPSHOT_COPIED_INTO_REPORT_SNAPSHOT.
classificationPerConsumer.notifications: NOT APPLICABLE — no reference to the analysis entity or table
classificationPerConsumer.executiveSummary: NOT APPLICABLE — no reference to the analysis entity or table
classificationPerConsumer.analytics: NOT APPLICABLE — no reference to the analysis entity or table

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.evidence: the ONLY production readers of HazLenzAnalysis are inspection.service.ts, the expert-hazlenz-product module, and entity relation declarations. reports, pdf, notifications, intelligence, action-engine and corrective-actions reference neither the entity nor the table.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.productOwnerQuestion: is transitive containment sufficient for a controlled beta? §266 recommends YES for the five, because four of them never read an analysis at all — but only once EXPERT_ANALYSIS_READABLE_OUTSIDE_THE_AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY is closed, since that is the one place the containment is a property of what happens to be written rather than of a guard.

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: The only GitHub workflow is frontend-e2e.yml. It sets working-directory: frontend, a directory that does not exist (the app is frontend-next), and triggers only on pull_request to main and workflow_dispatch.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.consequence: no automated verification runs on the beta branch or on a deploy
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.requiredAction: point it at frontend-next, or retire it and run hazlenz:precommit in CI

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: Expert transmits zero governed records, so it can cite nothing. Fail-closed by design.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.betaConsequence: Expert output carries no regulatory citation. The deterministic path still supplies standards, so the product is not citation-less — but Expert's contribution is hazard reasoning and posture only, which beta users should be told.

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: The Expert route runs its own deterministic analysis for Expert's premises; the inspector is looking at a separately persisted one. The two may diverge.
One settlement per analysis. A settled analysis cannot be re-opened.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.betaConsequence: a reviewer who settles wrongly cannot correct it. For a small, professionally competent cohort this is tolerable and worth learning from; it must be DISCLOSED rather than discovered.

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: 'HazLenz AI' now appears 202 times across the frontend (§256 counted 57). The core disclaimers on the main pages are materially correct and well-qualified.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.measuredGood: live copy already states HazLenz 'acts purely as a decision-support advisory tool', 'never auto-finalizes findings, declares violations, creates official citations, or replaces qualified safety professionals', and 'does not... determine compliance, or make final decisions'. §266 found NO claim that materially conflicts with accepted capability.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.residual: 'Every finding includes a full visual and step-by-step AI Reasoning Trace' is a completeness claim that should be checked against the Expert path, which surfaces no such trace.

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.note: §256 rated this P0. §266 records it as P1 FOR A CLOSED INVITED COHORT specifically: exposure scales with how public the beta is, and accepting the risk for a non-public cohort and recording that decision is a legitimate product-owner outcome. It returns to P0 before any public launch.

verdict.question: Is the current Safety InSite v1.0 product ready for a controlled human beta?
verdict.why: The safety-authority architecture is sound and proven: server-authored execution, deterministic admission, the persisted confirmation gate, human settlement, one effective-decision derivation and an activated downstream guard all hold under §262/§264/§265 evidence. What blocks beta is INTEGRATION and OPERATIONS: the shipped Expert client cannot execute at all against a real observation, a successful Expert run supersedes the customer-authoritative deterministic analysis, production has no migration mechanism, and no Terms or Privacy Policy exist. Every P0 below is finite and none requires redesign.
verdict.measuredNotInferred: §266 ran a read-only probe against a disposable database with a substituted transport and zero provider calls. P0-1, P0-2 and P0-3 are measured results, not code reading.
